review.summary:
I found one defect, and it affects both Rust and Swift. A nested block comment loses count of its depth. If a line inside an open comment has a `/*` but no `*/`, that `/*` is not counted. The cause is in `nestedEnd` (src/count.ts): when `line.indexOf(close)` is -1 it returns straight away with the depth unchanged, before checking for openers. As a result the comment ends one `*/` too early, and the lines after that point are counted as code.

I kept 2 failing tests in test/probe-a.test.ts. These cases passed, so I deleted their tests:
- **Rust:** nesting that closes and reopens on the same line; `/*/` and `/**/`; multi-line `br##"…"##`; character literals (`'\x41'`, `b'\''`, `'/'`, `'"'`, `'\u{10FFFF}'`); lifetimes and labels before a later char or comment; escapes over lines; `r"` after an identifier.
- **Swift:** `##"""…"""##` with `\##` escapes; `\#(x)` in `#"…"#`; `\"""` in `"""`; `#selector`.
- **Lua:** long strings and comments at different `=` levels; `--[[` inside strings; `f[[…]]`; `---[==[`; `- -1 --[[`.

findings.test: test/probe-a.test.ts > probe: nested block comments > counts a Rust /* opened on a line with no */ toward the nesting
findings.text: Rust block comments do not nest across lines when a line inside the comment opens another `/*` but has no `*/`. `nestedEnd` returns `{ end: -1, depth }` as soon as `indexOf(close)` is -1, so it never counts the `/*` openers on that line. Input: `/* 1` / `/* 2` / `/* 3 */ */` / `still` / `*/` / `x`. The depth should go 1→2→1→1→0, so only `x` is code (expected code 1, comments 5). Instead the depth stays at 1 after line 2, the comment closes on line 3, and `still` and `*/` are counted as code (got code 3, comments 3).

findings.test: test/probe-a.test.ts > probe: nested block comments > counts a Swift /* opened on a line with no */ toward the nesting
findings.text: Swift has the same defect, because it uses the same `nestedEnd`. Input: `/* a` / `/* b` / `*/` / `still` / `*/` / `let x = 1`. The comment should stay open until the second `*/` (expected code 1, comments 5). Instead the `/* b` opener is dropped, so the comment ends on line 3 and `still` and the final `*/` are counted as code (got code 3, comments 3).

failed: probe: nested block comments counts a Rust /* opened on a line with no */ toward the nesting
probe: nested block comments counts a Swift /* opened on a line with no */ toward the nesting
